investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 Causing Total Provisioning Failure Across All Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-01T01:13 with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 — was unreachable when the eval runner called POST /api/agents. Because the failure occurs at the very first API call before any evidence can be collected, all four required contract fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway backing the remote-agent provisioning path (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 reachable at the /v1/agents endpoint) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" for every attempt across all three sibling checks, preventing agent creation from starting and leaving the expected-output contract entirely unsatisfied. This is localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the remote-agents feature; no evidence of a broader production-api outage or user-traffic impact is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: Primary: The AWS ELB serving the swarm gateway /v1/agents endpoint in us-east-2 was down, unhealthy, or had no healthy targets at the time of the eval run, causing the production-api to return 502 for all agent provisioning requests.

Secondary: A transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api layer and the ELB in us-east-2 made the gateway unreachable for the duration of the eval window (~34 seconds across all three checks).
Tertiary: The swarm service behind the ELB was restarting, scaling down, or had crashed, leaving the ELB with zero healthy backends and returning 502 to all inbound requests.

Lower probability: A misconfigured or expired ELB listener rule or security group change blocked traffic to /v1/agents specifically, though the error message 'error sending request' suggests connection-level failure rather than an application-level rejection.

All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot JSON, not to the web surface itself.
investigations.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 746 minutes old when the eval executed, meaning the workflow was last triggered approximately 12.4 hours before the eval ran. This is an eval-detected operational gap in the snapshot-publishing pipeline, not a user-facing web outage — all public pages and routes remained reachable per sibling checks.

possibleCauses: Most likely: The GitHub Actions workflow that publishes the observability snapshot failed, was skipped, or was not scheduled to run for at least 746 minutes prior to the eval. The snapshot is structurally intact (source='github-actions', hasLiveSource=true) but was not refreshed on schedule.
Secondary: A GitHub Actions scheduling or runner availability issue caused the workflow to be queued but not executed within the expected cadence, resulting in the published snapshot going stale.
Secondary: The workflow ran but failed to push the updated snapshot to the GitHub Pages endpoint (https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json), leaving the old file in place.
Lower likelihood: A CDN or GitHub Pages caching layer is serving a stale version of status.json even though a newer file was published, causing the eval to read an outdated snapshotAgeMinutes value.
